subject: Capacity surge & renewal: 8→16 GPU upgrade — terms and throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + proposal: scale 8→16 GPUs with throughput SLOs

Hi Ethan —

Quick note as your renewal window opens: based on usage trends over the last 3 months we recommend moving from your current 8-GPU reserved pool to a 16-GPU reserved pool to hit the latency and throughput targets in your internal SLAs (esp. realtime scoring for Feature Store flushes).

Attached is an initial quote (GF-Quote-8to16-commit-2027-06.pdf) with two term options: 12-month and 24-month. Both include a baseline monthly commit (8→16) and an optional burst buffer for spiky batch jobs. We also outline a throughput SLO: 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms for seq len 512 at baseline load (details in throughput-profile-greenfield.csv).

High-level asks:
- Can you confirm target monthly throughput (tokens/month) or preferred spend band?
- Any constraints on term length or procurement cadence?
- Do you need credits or invoice timing to align with fiscal quarter close?

I’ve looped in Monica (CS) to validate migration timing and Laura (Sales Ops) for pricing. Happy to jump on a short call this week to walk the numbers.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: GF-Quote-8to16-commit-2027-06.pdf (proposal, 4 pages)
Attachment: throughput-profile-greenfield.csv (sample p95/p50 by seq len)
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greenfield.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@greenfield.ai>, Greenfield Procurement <procurement@greenfield.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + proposal: scale 8→16 GPUs with throughput SLOs

Thanks Connor — appreciate the proactive proposal. A few clarifying items from our side before we escalate to procurement: 

1) Baseline throughput: we currently average ~1.2B tokens/month with spikes to 2.8B during model retrain windows. We need to understand if the proposed monthly commit covers that or if burst credits are expected to absorb spikes.

2) Can you confirm the guaranteed p95 is for serving (inference) only, not for on-demand retrain jobs? Retrains can be scheduled but occasionally must run during business hours.

3) Pricing: the quote shows a per-month commit increase but there’s a footnote on overage rates and reserved vs burst pricing. Procurement will want a clear table of monthly commit, overage rate, and any carryover policy for unused commit.

4) Does Redwood support a short runway for capacity increase (e.g., add 4 GPUs mid-term if needed) and how does that affect pricing?

If you can provide a compact response we’ll route to procurement and legal.

—Ethan
VP of Platform Engineering, Greenfield Analytics
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + proposal: scale 8→16 GPUs with throughput SLOs

Hi Ethan — thanks for the details. Quick answers from CS/infra side: 

- The p95 <=120ms in the profile is scoped to inference (serving) at the pinned model variants. Retrain/large-batch training jobs are routed to a separate non-reserved pool by default; if you want retrains to hit the same latency SLOs they need to be included in the reserved capacity (we can model cost).

- Your token numbers look right for 16 GPUs as a baseline if you use our intelligent batching + KV cache settings. The burst buffer (configurable) covers short spikes up to ~40% extra throughput for up to 72 hours; anything beyond that would be billed at the overage rate.

- We support mid-term capacity adjustments. Adding 4 GPUs mid-term is possible with pro-rated commit adjustment and a 30-day activation window to re-provision; pricing would be the published rate for the remaining term, plus a one-time provisioning fee (line-itemed in the quote).

Marcus can share an example rollout timeline for a mid-July activation if that helps.

—Monica
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Greenfield Procurement <procurement@greenfield.ai>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal window + proposal: scale 8→16 GPUs with throughput SLOs

Hi procurement team — attaching a concise summary table to make sourcing easier.

Key terms (summary):
- Option A: 12-month term — monthly commit = 16 GPUs equivalent, monthly fee $82,500, overage rate $0.037/token equivalent, burst buffer included (up to 40% for 72 hours).
- Option B: 24-month term — monthly commit = 16 GPUs equivalent, monthly fee $76,500, overage rate $0.031/token equivalent, 6% annual price protection year 2.
- Mid-term adjustments: pro-rated commits with 30-day activation; one-time provisioning fee $3,500.
- Carryover policy: up to 10% of unused commit can roll to next month; no multi-month rollovers.
- SLA/credits: uptime 99.9%; below SLA we provide monthly service credits up to 25% of that month’s commit fee (as per standard SOW).

Attachments: GF-Quote-8to16-commit-2027-06.pdf (updated pricing table), throughput-profile-greenfield.csv

Let me know if you need a redline-friendly version for procurement/legal. We can also bake specific invoice timing into DocuSign.

—Laura
Manager, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greenfield.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenfield Procurement <procurement@greenfield.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + proposal: scale 8→16 GPUs with throughput SLOs

Thanks — that helps a lot. Procurement is comfortable moving forward with Option B (24 months) provided three small adjustments: 

1) Add a 45-day provisioning SLA for mid-term additions (so we can guarantee activation timelines).
2) Increase carryover cap to 15% to help smooth monthly batch variability.
3) Add explicit language that retrain jobs assigned to the reserved pool will be billed at the same per-GPU rate as serving when included in the commit.

If Redwood can accept those three edits we’ll sign via DocuSign and target an effective renewal date of 2027-07-01 with a phased capacity flip to 16 GPUs by 2027-07-15. Please share a redline and I’ll route to legal.

—Ethan
VP of Platform Engineering, Greenfield Analytics
